the potential for spontaneous recovery of the passive shoulder stabilizers, the ER peak torque deficit and the difference in ER and IR peak torque are the key determinants of the recovery of proprioception in IFS after arthroscopic capsular release.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the importance of the anatomical structure of the passive shoulder stabilizers and their potential for spontaneous healing for the recovery of proprioception and isokinetic muscle function of the rotator muscles.
the importance of passive stabilizers of the glenohumeral joint in the case of IFS and their relationship with shoulder proprioception and muscle performance.
the relationship between passive and active shoulder proprioception for IR and ER in IFS.

the anatomical structure of passive shoulder restraints and the potential for spontaneous recovery of the anterior and the posterior passive shoulder stabilizers have no influence on the recovery of passive shoulder proprioception, whereas the recovery of active shoulder proprioception is influenced by the recovery of the peak torque of external rotator muscles.
the potential for spontaneous recovery of the anterior and the posterior shoulder restraints influences proprioception and the isokinetic performance of the rotators.

the anatomical structure of the passive shoulder restraints (anterior and middle and inferior glenohumeral ligament and posterior capsule) influences the potential for spontaneous recovery of passive shoulder proprioception after arthroscopic IFS release, and that the peak torque deficit of external rotator muscles negatively affects the recovery of active shoulder proprioception after IFS release.Level of EvidenceII.

proprioception and muscle performance of the shoulder can be used as a prognostic tool for the outcome of arthroscopic IFS release.
proprioception is an important factor in shoulder pathology and that it is a useful tool in the assessment of shoulder disorders and the evaluation of the effectiveness of surgical treatment.
the potential for spontaneous recovery of anterior and posterior passive restraints has no effect on PJPS and AJP differences for ER and IR in IFS.

proprioception and isokinetic muscle function are not the same.
the potential for spontaneous recovery of passive shoulder stabilisers has a major impact on proprioception recovery after arthroscopy.
